messages:
sara_pm: Quick sync — need a final decision on graceful-degrade behavior for launch of the multitenant embeddings route. Customers pushing for deterministic latency but ops worried about cost spike. Proposal attached in PR but want alignment on acceptance criteria.

alex_eng: Thx. main tradeoff is: 1) strict p99 <= 250ms (may require shedding heavy contexts or switching models) vs 2) allow longer tails but keep lower fail-rate. Which is non-negotiable for launch?

matt_reliability: From reliability POV: we should define two orthogonal gates: Error budget burn (5% window) and p99 latency SLO. If error budget > 20% burn in the last 6h we trigger degraded mode automatically. We should also list allowed degrade actions in order.

li_devex: Suggested degrade actions (ranked): 1) prefix caching (serve cached KV if hit) 2) shorten context window (drop older turns) 3) switch to quantized model variant 4) return partial result with "truncated_due_to_load" flag 5) 429. Need to be explicit about acceptable user impact for each.

olivia_se: For enterprise customers on Dedicated, we should NOT 429 without first trying model switch or partial. SLA buyers expect graceful fallback options. Can we put a per-customer override?

alex_eng: Yes, config will be per-tenant. Rough config sketch in PR: 

```
fallback_policy:
  - name: prefix_cache
    max_stale_secs: 60
  - name: shorten_context
    min_context_tokens: 64
  - name: model_variant_switch
    target_model: "embed-quant-v2"
  - name: partial_response
    include_flag: true
  - name: throttling
    status: 429
```

sara_pm: This is helpful. For launch criteria I'd like the PRD acceptance checklist to require: "Automated degrade policy implemented + unit tests", "Canary shows <10% additional error burn vs baseline", "Runbook updated with steps and customer override flow." Agree?

matt_reliability: +1 but define canary duration and traffic slice. I'd propose 1% traffic for 48h, measure p50/p95/p99 and error budget burn. Stop if p99 regresses > 20% vs baseline or error burn > 10% in 30m.

li_devex: Also need e2e test for the partial response schema. Consumers must get a stable flag name and explanatory field. Add to acceptance: schema contract test.

olivia_se: Edge-case: long streaming requests where we shorten context mid-stream — how do we signal the client? We should avoid mid-stream model switch. Better to finish stream then degrade on next request. Add that to constraints.

alex_eng: Good call. We'll gate model switches to request boundaries. For streaming we can only drop caching and partial result fallback.

matt_reliability: One more: define rollback thresholds for rollout. I suggest automated rollback if canary p99 > 300ms for more than 15m or error burn > 5% within 15m. Include human in loop if enterprise customers affected.

sara_pm: Updated acceptance checklist in PR accordingly. I'll update the PR description with the canary and rollback thresholds. @deploy-bot can you create a canary job after merge?

deploy-bot: Canary job queued: topic=embeddings-degrade-canary, traffic=1%, duration=48h. See CI pipeline #7821.

li_devex: I'll add the contract test and a test vector set for partial responses. ETA EOD tomorrow.

olivia_se: I'll draft the customer-facing note about what degrade means for Dedicated customers.

alex_eng: I'll push the fallback policy change to the feature branch and add unit tests for gating logic.

sara_pm: Thanks team — plan: finalize PR today, merge with canary, and hold GA until canary passes. If anything urgent pops up ping me. :thumbsup:

matt_reliability: One follow-up: include telemetry events for each degrade action (event:degrade_action with fields action, reason, tenant, request_id) so we can audit and tie to error burn.

alex_eng: Will add events.

sara_pm: Great. Closing thread once PR merged.
